description: Panchayati Raj in India is a system of rural local self-government operating on the principle of democratic decentralisation. It was granted constitutional status through the landmark 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, adding Part IX to the Constitution.

sections.title: Historical Background and Major Committees
sections.description: The evolution of the Panchayati Raj system and the key Government of India committees that shaped its structural framework.

historical_events.event: Launch of Panchayati Raj in India
historical_events.significance: Inaugurated by the then Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru in Nagaur district, Rajasthan. Andhra Pradesh became the second state to implement it later that year.

key_associations.extra_info: Recommended a three-tier structure: Gram Panchayat at the village level, Panchayat Samiti at the block level, and Zila Parishad at the district level.
Recommended replacing the three-tier system with a two-tier system consisting of Zila Parishad and Mandal Panchayat. It was never implemented.
Recommended making the Zila Parishad the pivotal body in the scheme of democratic decentralisation and rural development.
Was the first committee to strongly recommend that Panchayati Raj institutions should be constitutionally recognized, protected, and preserved.

important_facts.fact: Lord Ripon is widely known as the 'Father of Local Self-Government in India' due to his famous Resolution of 1882 regarding local boards.

sections.title: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992
sections.description: This landmark act added a new Part IX (The Panchayats) and the 11th Schedule to the Constitution of India.

historical_events.significance: The amendment became effective across India on this day. Hence, April 24 is celebrated annually as 'National Panchayati Raj Day'.

key_concepts.explanation: Mandates a Gram Panchayat (Village level), Panchayat Samiti (Intermediate level), and Zila Parishad (District level). States with a population of less than 2 million may skip the intermediate level.
Mandates reservation for SCs and STs in proportion to their population. Also, a minimum of 1/3rd (33%) of the total seats and chairperson positions are reserved for women.
Panchayats have a fixed term of 5 years. If a Panchayat is dissolved prematurely, fresh elections must be held within 6 months of its dissolution.

sections.title: Important Constitutional Articles (Articles 243 to 243O)
sections.description: Key provisions enumerated under Part IX of the Indian Constitution detailing the functioning and structure of Panchayats.

polity_articles.details: Defines Gram Sabha as a village assembly consisting of all persons registered in the electoral rolls relating to a village comprised within the area of Panchayat.
Mandates the establishment of a three-tier Panchayati Raj system in every state.
Provides constitutional guarantee for the reservation of seats for SCs, STs, and Women across all three tiers.
Empowers Panchayats to prepare and implement plans for economic development and social justice, including the 29 subjects listed in the 11th Schedule.
Constituted by the Governor every 5 years to review the financial position of the Panchayats and recommend tax revenue distribution.
Responsible for the superintendence, direction, and control of the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of all Panchayat elections.

sections.title: 11th Schedule and the PESA Act
sections.description: Scope of work for Panchayats and the extension of these provisions to tribal and scheduled areas.

key_concepts.explanation: Contains 29 functional items placed within the purview of Panchayats, such as agriculture, land reforms, minor irrigation, rural electrification, and primary education.

key_concepts.concept: PESA Act 1996 (Panchayat Extension to Scheduled Areas Act)
key_concepts.explanation: Enacted on the recommendation of the Dileep Singh Bhuria Committee to extend the provisions of Part IX to the 5th Schedule Areas, thereby empowering tribal communities through Gram Sabhas.

important_facts.fact: The Panchayati Raj system does not apply to the states of Nagaland, Meghalaya, and Mizoram, which instead have traditional tribal councils.
Article 40 of the Constitution (Directive Principles of State Policy) directs the State to organize village panchayats and endow them with necessary powers.
The minimum age required to contest a Panchayat election is 21 years (unlike 25 years for the Lok Sabha or Legislative Assembly).
